# ARC downward shadow rule

## When to Use
Use when demo outputs recolor background cells in vertical columns beneath special-color source pixels.

When demos show a special-color pixel casting a vertical projection, determine trail color and stopping behavior from the examples. In the observed task, source-color markers cast trails of 3 through background cells. Fill straight gaps between successive same-color markers in a row or column, preserving all markers and other cells. Trails stop at markers and do not extend beyond the first/last marker in a line. The demonstrated examples used source color 5 or 1 over backgrounds 2; a test used source color 0 over background 9. Apply only when a straight row/column has at least two markers; fill cells strictly between consecutive markers with 3.

## Procedure
1. Compare source positions and output cells directly below in the same column.
2. Verify whether projections stop at another source pixel or continue to the edge; check whether original markers are preserved.
3. Apply only the demonstrated direction, trail color, and blockers; preserve unrelated cells.
4. Verify dimensions and stopping points before submission.

I’m considering how the output might have a band as the source shape, extending to the right edge in rows with gaps. In example 7, the rows look like broad bars. There's an isolated row that ends at column 15, and I'll recolor following it to the edge. Row 17 ends at column 16, so I’ll keep full rows unchanged due to there being no background on the right side.
